//: UAT / Staging. ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Staging selects this file. It contains NO secrets and no connection string, by design — see the two notes below. Local development uses appsettings.Development.json; production supplies everything through the environment and has no appsettings.Production.json at all.
//ConnectionStrings: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. The UAT connection string is a secret and arrives as the environment variable ConnectionStrings__Database, from the GitHub 'UAT' environment (or Key Vault once one exists). Adding a ConnectionStrings section here — even a placeholder — is how a real one eventually gets committed, so there is nothing here to fill in. The database it points at MUST be GymOS_UAT: DatabaseEnvironmentGuard refuses to boot a Staging host against any other database, and that mapping lives in code precisely so an environment variable cannot move it.

Database.//MigrateOnStartup: False everywhere, Staging included. The API runs as an application principal with no DDL rights, so it could not apply a migration even if asked — migrations are a separate deployment step running as the migrator principal (Database:MigrateOnly). See docs/Infrastructure/ENVIRONMENTS.md.

OpenApi.//Enabled: On in UAT, off in production. The base appsettings.json says the document is a complete map of every endpoint, parameter and schema, and names a staging or internal environment as exactly where publishing it is reasonable. QA and the console developers read it here rather than needing a local stack.

Serilog.//ConsoleFormat: JSON, because in a deployed environment these lines are read by a collector rather than a person — the same choice docker-compose.prod.yml makes for production.
